items.title: Water ingress is discovered late

blocks.title: Gateway-based deployment
blocks.body: For a compatible LoRa configuration, devices communicate with an agreed receiver or gateway and an onward platform connection. Check coverage among the racks at representative mounting points, including the effect of stored goods and metal structures.

data.h2: Set a baseline and define the response
data.p: Record the asset ID, mounting position, axes, initial readings and commissioning date. Keep measurement intervals and reporting intervals separate. Agree event handling, notification requirements and inspection responsibilities before the pilot is accepted.
bullets: An inclination reading describes local rotation where the sensor is mounted. It does not establish rack load capacity or replace a competent rack inspection.
Set review thresholds within the site's engineering and inspection process.
Notification timing depends on device configuration, network conditions and the platform workflow.

Retain the approved device configuration and point-location records for later installations.

faq.q: Does tilt monitoring tell us whether a rack is safe to load?
faq.a: No. An inclination reading describes local rotation at the mounting point and supports inspection prioritization and records. Rack safety assessment still requires load, design and a competent rack inspection.

faq.q: How many sensors does a warehouse need?
faq.a: There is no fixed number. The layout, rack types, zones and monitoring objectives define the points. Share your rack layout and we can review a suitable configuration together.

faq.q: Can the data go to our own platform?
faq.a: Integration is assessed for the selected device and platform. Share your endpoint, protocol, authentication and payload requirements so we can confirm the supported data path and test a sample message.

enquiry.h2: Share your rack layout and monitoring requirements.
enquiry.intro: Tell us the installation country, rack types, approximate monitoring points and preferred platform. A layout or site photo will help review mounting and coverage requirements.

blocks.title: Gateway-based within a station
blocks.body: Compatible LoRa devices report to a gateway that forwards data to the destination platform, suiting stations with several points in one building. Check coverage around pumps, pipework and metal structures.

blocks.title: Cellular for remote stations
blocks.body: Unattended or remote stations use 4G LTE or NB-IoT devices sending readings through a compatible mobile network, with no local gateway required.

data.p: Pressure, level, vibration and temperature readings are associated with assets and time, with thresholds agreed per operating range. Event handling and notification timing depend on device configuration, network conditions and the platform workflow.
bullets: Vibration trends support maintenance planning; they are not AI fault prediction.
Measurement, scheduled reporting and event handling are configured separately.
Data fields, units and timestamps are confirmed with the destination platform before deployment.

items: Confirm process connections and ranges for pressure and level points.
Mount vibration and temperature sensors at the agreed positions.
Check wireless coverage inside the station, including metal structures.
Record baseline readings, asset IDs and commissioning dates.
Test scheduled reports and the agreed notification workflow.

faq.q: Does pump vibration monitoring predict failures?
faq.a: No. The sensors provide vibration measurements, trends and threshold events within the supported band. Fault classification and remaining-life prediction are not claimed.

faq.q: Can remote stations run without local network infrastructure?
faq.a: Yes. Cellular 4G or NB-IoT devices send readings through a compatible mobile network. Confirm operator coverage at the station during the pilot.

faq.q: Which assets does a typical station configuration cover?
faq.a: Selected pump sets, inlet and outlet pipework, wet wells or tanks, and vulnerable floor areas. The point list is agreed per station.
